title: Jobs too big to share a resource

blocks.text: A transmission operator (not GridCap) plans its substation jobs for next season. Several limited resources are shared: the mobile crane's days, the outage hours the grid operator grants, the budget. Each is a knapsack row,

with $`x_j \in \{0, 1\}`$ (do job $`j`$), $`u_{\ell,j}`$ the whole amount of resource $`\ell`$ that job $`j`$ uses and $`U_\ell`$ what is available. `build` in `jobs.py` already writes these rows and the objective.

The planners noticed that some jobs are so big that no two of them fit under the same limit, and that the LP relaxation ignores this: it happily takes one big job and part of another. Write `add_big_item_rows(model, x, limits)`, which adds rows that

items: every whole plan that fits all the limits still satisfies (so no plan the limits allow is lost), and

stop the LP from combining big jobs: for each limit, the jobs no two of which fit together under it may be funded at most one at a time, and a job that does not fit under a limit even on its own is never funded, not even in part.

blocks.text: Each such row comes from a cover of one limit's row, a cover of two jobs or of one. Decide on paper which jobs belong to a limit's row, why "no two of them fit" is a simple test on each job's own use, and write the rows with their labels before coding. When a limit has only one big job, the reference writes no "at most one" row for it: that row would read $`x_j \le 1`$, which the variable's bound already says (a job too big even on its own still gets its "never" row).
The tests try every whole plan of five jobs against the limits, and compare the LP bound with the value the right rows give, so any correct set of valid rows passes. About seven lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from jobs import Limit, build

values = {"T1": 10, "T2": 6, "T3": 5, "T4": 4}
crane = Limit("crane_days", {"T1": 8, "T2": 7, "T3": 2, "T4": 3}, 12)
budget = Limit("budget", {"T1": 3, "T2": 3, "T3": 25, "T4": 4}, 20)


def lp_bound(limits):
    model, _ = build(values, limits, integer=False)
    return round(mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS).objective_value(), 3)


def best_plan(limits):
    model, _ = build(values, limits)
    return round(mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS).objective_value(), 3)


print("LP bound, crane only:", lp_bound([crane]))
print("best plan, crane only:", best_plan([crane]))
print("LP bound, crane and budget:", lp_bound([crane, budget]))
print("best plan, crane and budget:", best_plan([crane, budget]))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Limit:
    name: str
    use: dict          # job -> how much of this resource it uses (whole numbers)
    capacity: int


def add_big_item_rows(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, limits: list[Limit]) -> None:
    """Valid rows from the jobs too big to share a resource: at most one of them, none if alone too big."""
    # TODO: the valid rows that pairs of big jobs give.
    return None

def build(values: dict, limits: list[Limit], *, integer: bool = True) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="substation-jobs")
    x = {j: model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=1, is_integer=integer, name=f"x_{j}") for j in values}
    for lim in limits:
        model.add_linear_constraint(sum(u * x[j] for j, u in lim.use.items()) <= lim.capacity, name=lim.name)
    add_big_item_rows(model, x, limits)
    model.maximize(sum(v * x[j] for j, v in values.items()))
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    limits = [Limit("crane", {"J1": 7, "J2": 6, "J3": 2}, 10)]
    model, x = build({"J1": 5, "J2": 4, "J3": 1}, limits, integer=False)
    print(len(list(model.linear_constraints())), "rows")

cases.says: the jobs that each use more than half of a resource get one row allowing at most one of them, which lowers the LP bound and keeps every whole plan
every resource gives its own row over its own big jobs
two jobs using exactly half a resource each fit together, so no row may forbid that pair
a job using more than all of a resource is held at 0, so the LP cannot fund part of it

origin.section: A Cover Row Cuts Off LP Points the Budget Row Allows

concepts: a cover row removes fractional LP points the knapsack row allows and keeps every whole plan
a set of items whose weights exceed the capacity gives a row that every whole plan obeys
